artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a permutation $w \in S_n$, let $\mathfrak{S}_w(x_1, \dots, x_{n-1})$ denote its Schubert polynomial, and define
$$\nu_w := \mathfrak{S}_w(1, 1, \dots, 1),$$
the sum of the coefficients of $\mathfrak{S}_w$ (equivalently, the principal specialization at all variables equal to $1$). Call a permutation $w \in S_n$ \emph{layered} if there exist integers $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k = n$ such that, in one-line notation,
$$w = (i_1, i_1-1, \dots, 2, 1,\; i_2, i_2-1, \dots, i_1+1,\; i_3, i_3-1, \dots, i_2+1,\; \dots,\; i_k, i_k-1, \dots, i_{k-1}+1).$$
Prove that for every $n \ge 1$, every permutation $w \in S_n$ that maximizes $\nu_w$ over $S_n$ is a layered permutation.
artifact.status_search_result: The Merzon–Smirnov conjecture (2015) that the maximum of the principal specialization $\nu_w = \mathfrak{S}_w(1,\dots,1)$ over $S_n$ is attained only by layered permutations remains open. Morales–Pak–Panova determined the maximum among layered permutations and the asymptotics, and subsequent work has produced highly non-layered families with very large principal specializations, but no proof of the full conjecture has appeared.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics of principal evaluations of Schubert polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Stanley asked... it is conjectured by Merzon and Smirnov that such w must be layered. Assuming that w is layered, Morales, Pak and Panova determined such w's that achieve the maximum value.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is attributed to Merzon–Smirnov and the maximum among layered permutations is known, while the full conjecture is stated as open.

status_evidence.title: Principal specializations of Schubert polynomials, multi-layered permutations and asymptotics
status_evidence.snippet: Large families of permutations very far from being layered achieve extremely large principal specializations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work indicates the conjecture remains open and may be subtle, as non-layered permutations can come close to the maximum.
